findings.issue: Deny-to-allow against main (the branch point) in the history guard. `parts_read_alone` now sends a command to the text reading whenever any part ends open in `_config`'s walk, including commands whose RAW joined view main tokenized and graded as operations. The text reading cannot see parse-only spellings: a quoted verb or program word, which `_GIT_SUB`/`_STASH` require bare, and `xargs git`, whose STDIN_VERB refusal in `decide` reads `calls or []` and so never fires on the text reading. Measured over scratch exports of main, HEAD and HEAD with this diff, calling `decide` on a repo with a plan and a recorded SHA: deny on main and on HEAD, allow with this diff, for <QUOTED-STASH-DROP> (the stash-drop verb with its verb word double-quoted), <QUOTED-PROGRAM-STASH-DROP> (the program word quoted), <QUOTED-FORCE-PUSH> and <XARGS-GIT> (a verb piped to `xargs git`), placed in the text beside: a shell body whose last line ends in a backslash (`bash <<'X'` / `echo a` + backslash / `X`, verb before or after it); a body that opens a quote a later body closes (single, double, backquote or `$(`); a glued `#'` body plus a closing body; a text ending in a backslash after a body (quoted stash drop only); and an `echo "$(` body closed by a later body. 98 history rows are weaker than main; once the deliberate allows and the rows HEAD already had are removed, these shapes are what is left, and none of them uses a plain verb. Plain spellings (<STASH-DROP>, <FORCE-PUSH>, <HARD-RESET>, `git -C` forms) are never weaker than main or HEAD. Main parsed these lines correctly because the verb sat in a part the open quote did not reach. The task asked for exactly this routing ('send the command to the strict text reading over the whole view'), so the gap comes from that routing combined with the text reading's existing blindness. Main already allowed the same spellings when the whole line failed to tokenize (`<QUOTED-STASH-DROP>; echo '`). What this diff adds is the set of lines that main read as operations and that now reach that blindness.
findings.resolution: Keep the strict reading, and keep the parse of the parts that can be read. When `parts_read_alone` fails, collect `git_calls` of every part that ends closed and tokenizes alone. Grade those calls in each arm's None branch (`always_refused`, `amend_requested`, `stash_operations`, `reset_targets`) and in `decide`'s STDIN_VERB check, in addition to the text patterns, so that a verb main read as an operation is still read as one. Add deny cases to tests/test_guard_history_rewrite.py for <QUOTED-STASH-DROP> and <XARGS-GIT> beside the trailing-backslash body and beside the open/close body pair. Each case should be red on this diff and green on main.

findings.issue: s81-s83 (added by this task) and s79/s80 (inherited) cannot go red on the behaviour their comments name. The s81 comment says the case guards against 'a closer, which would make the read line the inside of a quote', and the s79 comment says 'the pair locks it through the runnable view'. Alternatively, point a case at a secrets arm that parses the joined view (`_manifest_write_placed`, `_source_write_hit` and `_past_bound_writers` read `runnable`) and show that it goes red when a part's open quote carries into the next.

preExisting.issue: Weaker than main already at HEAD, so not this diff: a house-form message that a later clause executes. `git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF' / <STASH-DROP> / EOF / )" ; bash -c "$(git log -1 --format=%B)"` and `git tag -m <house body: FORCE-PUSH> v1 && git tag -l -n1 v1 | sh` are denied on main and allowed on HEAD and with this diff, by the history, secrets (with a secret read as the body), uncommitted and release guards. Also the `\r#'` body followed by a body that runs <QUOTED-STASH-DROP> (history guard: deny on main, allow on HEAD).
preExisting.resolution: Do not lift a house body when another clause of the same command re-reads the commit or tag message (`git log --format=%B`, `git tag -l -n`) into a shell; grade it as text instead.

preExisting.issue: Equal on main, HEAD and this diff, and noted by the executor: a shell body holding TWO nested quoted heredocs with apostrophes (an even count) runs <STASH-DROP>/<FORCE-PUSH>/<HARD-RESET>/<TAG> unrefused by every guard, because the two misread quotes pair up inside one part. guard-release also finds no tag in any nested-heredoc shell body on any of the three trees.
preExisting.resolution: Make split_heredocs read nested heredocs inside a shell body.
